sources.name: USDA Forest Service EDW Recreation Opportunities GIS — White Bridge Picnic Site, recarea 77748
observations: Feature objectid 9740 / recarea 77748 identifies White Bridge Picnic Site. Its WGS84 geometry is approximately 34.5495443,-111.8506131 and published coordinate attributes are 34.549539,-111.850602.

The official description says the developed site provides access to the Verde River and non-motorized boating. The linked Forest Service photos describe a trail from the picnic area to the river and a paved portion of that trail.
The feature point is about 63 feet from the former route coordinate.
sources.limits: This managed recreation-site point locates the picnic/boating access area, not a surveyed shoreline toe or a seasonally verified launch location.

sources.name: Forest Service — Verde River Paddle Trail guide
observations: The guide describes White Bridge RAP as a heavily used Forest Service access just below the Highway 260 bridge, with restrooms, picnic tables, and ramadas.
Its waypoint table lists White Bridge RAP at 34.5511,-111.8508, approximately 573 feet north of the current Forest Service recreation-site feature.
The same publication says its maps are for reference use and map accuracy is not guaranteed.
sources.limits: The guide's waypoint is approximate and conflicts with the current recreation-site GIS marker; it does not identify the exact wet toe.

sources.name: Friends of the Verde River — Verde River Access Points map
observations: The access table labels the former stored coordinate, 34.5496,-111.8508, as White Bridge at river mile 76.2, matching the Forest Service picnic-site marker to about 63 feet.
sources.limits: This independent river access map supports the named RAP and nearby access location, but does not state that the table coordinate is a surveyed wet toe.

sources.name: USGS National Hydrography Dataset Large Scale — refreshed targeted route-distance audits
observations: Across all five refreshed routes, White Bridge is 200–406 feet from the matched Verde River flowline and about 2,406 feet from the nearest mapped waterbody feature.
All five targeted route audits completed with zero source issues; all five classify the site marker as review.
sources.limits: The waterbody layer does not resolve the wet toe here; hydrography is not public-access or shoreline-entry evidence.

decision: Use the current official Forest Service recreation-site marker for the White Bridge public picnic/boating access area; retain review status because the precise launch toe is not independently mapped.
